title: Four Things We Learned From USMNT’s Perfect World Cup Response
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Amanda Langell3:30 PM EDTThe USMNT bounced back from the World Cup with four straight wins. / Rich Storry/Getty ImagesThree months ago, the U.S. men’s national team was standing in front of a disappointed crowd in Seattle, heads hanging low after a humiliating World Cup exit to Belgium.

Mauricio Pochettino’s squad, often heralded as the “golden generation” of American players, crashed out of the showpiece event in the round of 16 after a lopsided 4–1 defeat. The loss was the cure to the soccer fever taking over the United States this summer—but not for long.

A new-look roster, featuring eight teenagers and led by new captain Tyler Adams, represented the Stars and Stripes during the September-October international break and once again captured the attention of the nation with four strong wins against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada.

History was made along the way and stars were born during the faultless run this fall. Pochettino also learned some valuable lessons that could shape how the 2030 World Cup cycle unfolds for the USMNT.

Christian Pulisic was left off Mauricio Pochettino’s roster. / Alex Grimm/Getty ImagesMuch was made about Pochettino’s head-turning omissions before the international window got underway. The Argentine boss left Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun at home, three mainstays of the team.

For so long, Pulisic and Co. were expected to unlock the best version of the USMNT. The common perception was if they weren’t donning red, white and blue, the team stood little chance of overcoming solid opposition.

Yet with a newly blended squad of youth and veterans, the Stars and Stripes did more than just overcome solid opposition—they dominated their opponents. Pochettino’s men scored 12 goals and conceded just three in four consecutive victories, all without the three biggest names on the team.

Instead of making the same mistakes as his predecessors, Pochettino put his faith in other talents and was rewarded immensely. The Argentine got more from his debutants in the final third than he has from Pulisic throughout his entire time in charge of the USMNT. Had Pochettino forced the out-of-form AC Milan star into his XI, he could have witnessed much different score lines this fall.

What this says about Pulisic’s future with the team remains to be seen, but the burden is now on the American to prove himself worthy of a call-up; the Stars and Stripes are no longer desperate for his services.
The USMNT are handing the keys to the kids. pic.twitter.com/cpWbBzfEFb

Leaving home veterans made room for a wealth of youngsters to stake their claim with the USMNT—and they did just that. Cavan Sullivan, Julian Hall and Justin Ellis found the back of the net a combined six times, accounting for half the team’s goals this international break.

Sullivan became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history at 17 years and five days old, while Hall became only the third American player to score in three consecutive international games. The 18-year-old also is the youngest player to reach the milestone since the legendary Pelé did so for Brazil in 1957 at age 16.

Seventeen-year-old Mathis Albert found the back of the net as well, opening his account in just his second-ever appearance for the Stars and Stripes. Peyton Miller also showed his worth at left back, impressing in his one start against Peru.

There will be bigger tests for the youngsters to come, especially once the USMNT faces European opposition on the road to the 2030 World Cup, but Pochettino has a group of teenagers who look ready for the challenge.

Tyler Adams is the new leader of the USMNT. / Omar Vega/USSF/Getty ImagesThe captain’s armband was not left vacant for long following Tim Ream’s retirement. Pochettino handed the honor to Adams, who previously captained the USMNT at the 2022 World Cup.

“I think he knows what I expect,” Pochettino said of Adams, “and he’s a perfect role model for everyone in the way that the philosophy, the future, representing that amazing country ... He’s the player and the person that can lead that period that we have ahead.”

Adams is indeed a natural leader. The 27-year-old comes with 62 international caps to his name—a number only that low due to multiple injury issues over the years—and has the unique experience of playing in MLS, the Bundesliga and now the Premier League. He can relate to many of the young stars filling out Pochettino’s ranks and is an exemplary model for how to conduct himself on and off the pitch.

The Bournemouth standout, who was one of the few USMNT veterans to play in the 2025 Gold Cup, is calm under pressure, relentless out of possession and willing to do all the dirty work in midfield. Adams showed as much in his elite performances against Peru and Mexico, in which he highlighted  his accurate passing as well.

Even when he came off the bench against Chile and Canada, he hardly put a foot wrong and helped the team close out both victories without any late drama. The ability to lead a new-look, inexperienced team to four consecutive victories cast away any doubt of his leadership abilities.
